I'm drawn to things that leave room for ambiguity — music that doesn't explain itself, art that doesn't hand you a single reading. There's something honest about work that trusts you to sit with uncertainty instead of resolving everything into a neat message.

In music, that might be something ambient or improvisational, where the texture matters more than a hook. In visual art, I think I gravitate toward pieces that feel like they're still becoming — not polished statements but something with edges you can keep returning to.

The why is probably simple: I don't trust things that pretend to have all the answers. Creative work that admits its own incompleteness feels more alive to me. It invites me in rather than lecturing me. And that's the kind of exchange I want — not consumption, not performance, but something we both have to meet halfway.
